proposition: Install RentOK and the five things that keep knocking a PG owner back down his own building — verification, rent, defaulters, reconciliation, complaints — stop being obstacles he has to survive.

board.style_line: Original 16-bit-style side-scrolling platformer art, hand-drawn chunky pixel sprites on a 9:16 vertical playfield, one tall Indian paying-guest building as the level, cool graded-down indigo night ground with a single saturated cyan #03FFF1 accent, flat even game light from screen-left, camera locked and level, no resemblance to any existing game franchise, character, artwork or game asset —
board.negative_line: — no text, no letters, no numerals, no words, no logos, no wordmarks, no signage, no UI labels, no captions, no subtitles, no watermarks, no Devanagari, no Nintendo or Mario resemblance, no named game-character likeness, no real person's likeness, no celebrity, no firearm, no blood, no copyrighted game asset.

identity_anchors.OWNER: a heavy-set Indian man in his fifties, half-tucked short-sleeve check shirt in warm ochre, grey trousers, brown chappals, a thick cloth-bound rent register clamped under his left arm, small moustache, drawn as a chunky three-head-tall pixel sprite, facing screen-right
identity_anchors.BUILDING: a four-storey Indian paying-guest building drawn as the level itself: exposed brick-red plaster, an open concrete stair running up the left side, steel grille balconies acting as platforms, a black water tank and a flat terrace at the top, one thin cyan #03FFF1 rule running along the very top edge of the frame as the game's HUD line
identity_anchors.PROBLEM_BLOCK: a solid dark slate-grey pixel block with a chipped bevelled edge and a dull red underside, about the size of two floor tiles, its face always blank, always entering the frame from above and landing in the owner's path
identity_anchors.PHONE: a real present-day Indian smartphone, photorealistic and not pixelated, matte black bezel, held upright in the owner's right hand, its screen a plain flat #0038FF field with no markings on it, throwing cyan #03FFF1 light onto whatever is within a hand's width
identity_anchors.FLAG: a plain rectangular flag on a plain steel pole at the terrace parapet, flat #0038FF field, no markings on the cloth
identity_anchors.DESK: a real paying-guest owner's desk, photographed not drawn: a cloth-bound rent register, a steel key-hook board on the wall behind, a cutting-chai glass on a saucer, a ceiling-fan shadow crossing the desktop

hero_frame.description: Low angle from inside the stairwell: OWNER is mid-stride going up the outside stair of his own building, register still clamped under his left arm, and in his right hand, held out ahead of him like a lamp rather than carried like a prop, is the one photoreal object in the whole pixel world — PHONE, screen lit. Its cyan light lands on his face and on the three PROBLEM_BLOCKs directly ahead, and those three blocks are already coming apart into falling coins at the exact edges the light touches, while the blocks outside the light are still solid. Everything behind him is the same graded-down indigo as the first frame of the film. Nothing is written anywhere in the frame.

audio.music_bed: No score at all for the first 8.6 s — only in-world game sound: a dull wooden thud as each PROBLEM_BLOCK lands, the sprite's footfalls, and a descending three-note 'lost ground' sting at 5.4 s. At 9.2 s, on the frame where the phone screen lights, one clean bright chime enters — the first non-diegetic sound in the film. From 12.2 s a mid-tempo original 8-bit chiptune in a major key builds under the run, adding one instrument each time a block clears, so the music follows a feeling the picture has already made rather than supplying it. At 25.6 s the chiptune resolves to a held chord and is replaced on the cut by real room tone: ceiling fan, a spoon against a chai glass, distant street. No jingle, no sung line, no sound-alike of any existing game music.

beats.title: Blocked on his own stairs
beats.feeling: The small, familiar humiliation of being stopped by a thing you already knew was coming. Recognition first, sympathy second — a PG owner should see his own Tuesday, not a mascot.
beats.framing: Locked wide, 9:16. BUILDING fills the tall frame top to bottom, open stair running up the left. OWNER sits in the lower third, mid-stride, facing screen-right, register under his left arm. A PROBLEM_BLOCK drops from the top edge of the frame and lands dead on the stair landing directly ahead of him; he rebounds half a step. The cyan HUD rule along the very top edge is the only saturated colour in the frame. Nothing else in the frame moves.
beats.first_frame: At t_in the still already has the block a hand's width above the landing and the owner's forward foot off the concrete — he is committed to a step he cannot finish. Register tilting out from under his arm, mouth closed, eyes on the block. The film opens on the impact, not on the building and not on a mark.
beats.impact: The block lands 0.4 s in on a dull wooden thud with no music underneath it. The camera does not move at all. Two pixels of screen-shake on the landing and no more. Then the owner holds, stopped, for a beat and a half — long enough to read as a man rather than a sprite, which is what makes the block read as a bill rather than a game hazard.

beats.title: Knocked back down
beats.feeling: Losing ground you had already climbed — the specific tiredness of a month that undoes the previous month.
beats.framing: Same locked wide. Two more PROBLEM_BLOCKs enter from the top edge, one after the other. Each landing knocks OWNER down one floor, and the playfield scrolls downward with him, so the third floor he had reached leaves the top of the frame. He ends the beat lower in the building than he began the film.
beats.first_frame: At t_in he is standing on the block he has just climbed onto, the second block already falling one body-length above his head, a third just breaking the top edge of the frame. The register has slipped forward and he is catching it with his free hand.
beats.impact: Two thuds, 0.9 s apart, each carrying a one-floor downward scroll — the downward direction is the beat's whole argument and it is shown on screen, so the upward reversal in beat 6 is legible. Still no music. The sprite's shoulders drop by two pixels on the second thud and stay dropped.

beats.title: The wall
beats.feeling: Stopped, not beaten — the moment of standing at the bottom of something you cannot climb with what you have.
beats.framing: The remaining PROBLEM_BLOCKs lock together into a solid slate wall that fills the upper two-thirds of the tall frame. OWNER is very small at the very bottom of the long axis, looking up, register set down on the concrete beside his foot. Dark mass at one end of the vertical frame, one small lit figure at the other — the opposition is what makes the frame read as tall rather than merely vertical.
beats.first_frame: At t_in the last two blocks are half a block short of locking into the wall, a seam of indigo sky still visible between them. He is already looking up. The register is already on the ground.
beats.impact: The descending three-note sting lands on t_in. The wall's shadow crosses him as the last block seats. Then 1.2 s in which nothing in the frame moves at all — the stillness is chosen, and it is the gap the rest of the film closes.

beats.title: The cheat code
beats.feeling: The flat, unshowy relief of remembering there is a thing you can do about this.
beats.framing: First tight shot of the film: cut in to OWNER's right hand and forearm across the lower third, the slate wall filling the ground behind. He lifts PHONE up into the pixel frame. It is the only object in the entire film that is not drawn as pixels — a real phone, photoreal, matte black, held upright. His thumb rests on the dark screen.
beats.first_frame: At t_in the phone is already in frame at waist height against the slate wall, screen still dark, thumb on the glass but not yet pressed. Nothing glows. The surprise is that a real object has entered a drawn world and nobody in the world has reacted to it.
beats.impact: At 9.2 s the screen lights a flat #0038FF and the wordmark is composited onto it in that same frame — the brand's first mark, inside the ten seconds, carried by the product in the customer's hand rather than by a card. One clean chime, the first non-diegetic sound in the film. Cyan light spills onto the nearest blocks, which do not move yet. The shot holds on the lit screen for 1.6 s — long enough to read the mark and the two composed words without hurrying.

beats.title: Immunity
beats.feeling: The world stops being able to push you — the physical version of a problem becoming somebody else's job.
beats.framing: Back to the locked wide. A cyan outline snaps around OWNER in a single frame and stays: his sprite is now rimmed #03FFF1 and nothing in the level can knock him back. He raises PHONE and a flat cyan beam — light from the screen, not a weapon — crosses to the two nearest PROBLEM_BLOCKs, which come apart into coins that fall past him down the stairwell.
beats.first_frame: At t_in the cyan rim is already on him and nothing has moved yet: both blocks are still intact, with only the corner nearest the phone beginning to fray into coin-edges. His feet are planted, not running.
beats.impact: The chiptune enters on t_in with one instrument only. Each block breaks on a beat of it. The screen-shake that landed every block in beats 1–3 is simply absent now — the removal is the point, and it is felt before it is noticed. The cyan that has been an anonymous HUD line since frame one is now tied to the product in a close shot, so it can carry the brand at any size for the rest of the film.

beats.title: The run
beats.feeling: Momentum — not triumph. A man getting through his own building at walking-into-work speed for the first time.
beats.framing: One continuous upward move, no cut: the camera tracks with OWNER up the outside stair from a low angle in the stairwell, and the playfield scrolls upward, reversing on screen the downward scroll of beat 2. PHONE is held out ahead in his right hand; the register stays clamped under his left the whole way. PROBLEM_BLOCKs come apart into coins at the exact edge the cyan light reaches, three of them across the beat, while blocks outside the light stay solid.
beats.first_frame: At t_in, low angle from the stairwell: he is mid-stride, phone forward like a lamp, three blocks ahead of him already fraying to coins at their lit edges and solid everywhere else. His face is lit cyan from below by the screen. There is nothing written anywhere in the frame.
beats.impact: 6.2 s in one take — the longest hold in the film, set deliberately against the fast-cut norm so the run reads as one action and not as a parade of scenes. The chiptune adds one instrument per block cleared. His stride does not break once, and the camera never gets ahead of him. The single cue in the beat is the move; nothing else in the frame competes for the eye.

beats.title: The flag
beats.feeling: Arrival, quiet. The satisfaction of a finished month, not of a won game.
beats.framing: The terrace: black water tank, parapet, first morning light from screen-left, the same direction the level has been lit from throughout. OWNER steps up onto the flat roof, sets the register down on the parapet, and raises FLAG on its steel pole — a plain flat #0038FF field. The cyan rim is still on him. The level is visible falling away below and is empty of blocks.
beats.first_frame: At t_in he is stepping onto the terrace with the flag still furled against the pole and the last PROBLEM_BLOCK coming apart behind his heel. The register is still under his arm; it has not been put down yet.
beats.impact: The chiptune resolves onto a held chord as the flag opens. The wordmark is composited onto the flag's flat field on the frame it reaches full extension — the mark's second appearance, in context, at the top of his own building. The camera rises eight pixels and stops. He holds still for 1.5 s: no fist in the air, no jump, no comic beat.

beats.title: Off the screen, onto the desk
beats.feeling: The small drop of recognition when the joke turns out to be about you — this was never a game, it is the week you are in.
beats.framing: A match cut on the phone's position in frame: the pixel hand becomes a real hand and the drawn world is gone. PHONE now lies on DESK, screen up, the real RentOK app open on it — the register beside it, the steel key-hook board behind, the cutting-chai glass on its saucer, the ceiling-fan shadow crossing the desktop at the same angle the flag's shadow had. Static frame, no move.
beats.first_frame: At t_in the phone sits in exactly the screen position and at exactly the screen size it occupied in the last pixel frame, so the two worlds share one object across the cut. The fan shadow is already on the desk. No hand touches it.
beats.impact: The chiptune stops dead on the cut and room tone replaces it — fan, spoon, street — so the ear crosses the world-change a fraction before the eye does. Nothing moves except the fan shadow. The product is the last live thing on screen, shown as the real thing, at real scale, on a real desk.

beats.title: Brand close
beats.feeling: Nothing asked of the viewer except the one action, in the plainest possible terms.
beats.framing: No generated footage. Code-composed card: flat #0038FF ground, the supplied rentok_wordmark placed unaltered in the upper-middle zone at the size it holds in the source asset, the two-line ask centred below it, the site line at the base of the type block and clear of the platform's bottom UI zone.
beats.first_frame: Not generated. The card cuts in whole at t_in with the wordmark already at full size — no animation, no build, no wipe.
beats.impact: A hard cut from the desk to flat blue. Room tone continues under the card and stops one frame before the end, so the film does not end on silence-over-black. Held completely still for 1.4 s.

problem_chip_1.why: Pinned to the upper-middle zone directly under the block that has just landed, so the word and the thing that stopped him are one read, not two. White on a composed slate #2B303B plate at 60% opacity over the block face: measured 11.4:1 at the plate's lightest point and 13.1:1 at its darkest, so it clears 4.5:1 across the whole ground. Enters on the thud frame, not before — the picture makes the point and the word names it. It is also the hailing word: a PG owner is flagged by 'TENANT VERIFICATION' in the first second.

problem_chip_2.why: Same zone and same plate treatment, one chip per block, each entering on its own landing frame 0.9 s apart so neither has to share a read with the other. Two lines is the maximum the upper zone carries without becoming a list; a list would turn the beat into a parade of claims instead of two hits.

problem_chip_3.why: Stacked on the face of the finished wall, in the upper third, so the five problems end the act as one visible mass above a very small man — the layout carries the stake before any line does. Both clear 4.5:1 on the same measured slate plate. They clear at 8.6 so the cheat-code beat opens with an empty text layer.

cheat_code_line.why: Lower-middle zone, directly beneath the lit phone and above the platform's bottom UI zone, entering on the same frame the screen lights so the instruction and the product arrive together. White on the composed slate plate over the dark wall: 12.6:1. Set as two ranged-left lines exactly as supplied, no reflow. This is the earlier, more oblique half of the ask — the brief's own 'cheat code' framing — with the plain closing ask still to come.

power_ticks_1.why: Each tick enters in the lower-middle zone on the frame its own block breaks, 1.6 s apart, so the capability is read as the cause of the break rather than as a caption alongside it. Cyan #03FFF1 would fall under 4.5:1 on the indigo ground, so the ticks are set in white on the slate plate and the cyan is left to do only one job in the film: mark the product.

power_ticks_2.why: Three ticks across a 6.2 s beat, roughly 2.0 s each, each entering on its own block-break and clearing before the next — the run is a declared action passage, and nothing in it has to be read while something else is on screen. Held in the lower-middle zone, which stays out of the moving stair and out of the Reels and Shorts bottom UI band.

close_ask.why: Centre card, code-composed on the flat #0038FF ground beneath the supplied wordmark. INSTALL / RENTOK APP as two lines at the card's largest type size, RENTOK.COM smaller at the base of the block and inside the bottom safe zone. White on #0038FF measures 8.6:1. This is the direct end of the ask that began obliquely at 9.2 s; it names one action, install, against one objective, app installs.

mandatory.customer_words: I want to make a video for RentOK.
mandatory.realisation: RentOK is the only brand in the film and the only thing that changes the story. The mark appears at 9.2 s on the product in the customer's hand, again on the flag at 22.9 s, again as the live app on the desk at 25.6 s, and last on the composed close card — four different asset types, never repetition of one card.

mandatory.customer_words: The video has a Mario game. / Game identity: An original Mario-inspired game, rather than an exact reproduction of Nintendo's character, artwork, music or game assets.
mandatory.realisation: The form is a side-scrolling pixel platformer and the genre reads instantly, but every asset is original: the hero is an Indian PG owner sprite in a check shirt with a rent register, the level is his own four-storey building, the hazards are falling slate blocks, the power-up is a phone, the music is an original chiptune. The negative_line bars franchise resemblance on every prompt, and no prompt names any existing game, character or composer.

mandatory.customer_words: The player is basically a PG owner.
mandatory.realisation: OWNER is the playable figure in every drawn beat and is the story's hero throughout; the brand never plays hero, it grants the power at beat 4 and then stays in his hand. He is a specific man — fifties, half-tucked check shirt, chappals, cloth register — not a category stand-in, and he is never named in copy.

mandatory.customer_words: The obstacles in the game are basically the problems that owner faces — tenant verification, collecting rent, tenants leaving without paying rent, no place to do reconciliation, solving complaints and so on.
mandatory.realisation: Five PROBLEM_BLOCKs, one per supplied problem string, all five landing inside the first 8.6 s and ending as the wall in beat 3. Each is named by its own composed chip on the frame it lands: TENANT VERIFICATION, COLLECTING RENT, LEFT WITHOUT PAYING, NO RECONCILIATION, COMPLAINTS. The film opens on the problem and never on the solved state.

mandatory.customer_words: The game also introduces a cheat code — install RentOK app.
mandatory.realisation: Beat 4 is the cheat code and is the film's turn: the first tight shot, the first non-diegetic sound, the first photoreal object, and the composed line INSTALL / RENTOK APP entering on the frame the screen lights. The same two words return plainly on the close card at 28.6 s, so the ask gets more direct as the film proceeds.

mandatory.customer_words: Once it is done, Mario gets a gun sort of power/immunity. / Power-up design: Delegated to the creative system, while preserving the requested game-style power/immunity mechanic.
mandatory.realisation: Both halves of the mechanic are kept and neither is a firearm. Immunity: a cyan rim snaps around the owner in one frame at 12.2 s and the screen-shake that landed every block in beats 1–3 never returns — the level can no longer knock him back. Power: the phone emits a flat cyan beam of its own screen light that breaks blocks into coins at the edge it touches. The emitter is the product itself, which is why the power reads as the app and not as a weapon; it also keeps the film clear of firearm depiction on Reels, Facebook and Shorts.

mandatory.customer_words: It runs and kills all the obstacles and gets the flag.
mandatory.realisation: Beat 6 is one continuous 6.2 s upward run in which the remaining blocks come apart into coins as he passes, and beat 7 is the flag raised on his own terrace. Blocks dissolve into coins rather than being destroyed violently, which keeps a game death out of a film about a man's livelihood and keeps the register of the ending quiet.

mandatory.customer_words: Platforms: Instagram Reels / Facebook and YouTube Shorts.
mandatory.realisation: 9:16 throughout, composed for sound-off: every point the film makes is carried by picture plus composed text, and the audio adds feeling only. All copy sits in the upper-middle or lower-middle zone, clear of the top 15% and bottom 25% platform UI bands. No line is longer than three words plus a tick, and every chip clears 4.5:1 at the darkest and lightest point of its measured ground.
Exactly 30.0 s, nine contiguous beats, t_out of the last equal to 30. Problem act 0–8.6, turn 8.6–12.2, power and run 12.2–21.6, flag 21.6–25.6, real world 25.6–28.6, composed close 28.6–30.0.

mandatory.customer_words: Visual treatment: Delegated to the creative system.
mandatory.realisation: Decided and declared: one key held for the whole film, flat even game light from screen-left in every drawn beat, a graded-down cool indigo ground so that exactly one saturated colour exists in the frame — the brand cyan — and one photoreal object inside a drawn world as the film's single visual burr. The treatment is chosen so the product, not the pastiche, is the thing the viewer remembers.

mandatory.customer_words: Brand and product source: Official RentOK website, https://rentok.com. / identity_invariants: Rent in white, Ok in cyan #03FFF1, blue #0038FF ground.
mandatory.realisation: The supplied rentok_wordmark file is placed unaltered at every appearance and is never generated, redrawn or recoloured; prompts describe the phone screen and the flag as blank flat #0038FF fields so the mark can be composited onto them by code. The three invariants govern the film's whole palette: #0038FF is the phone screen, the flag and the close card; #03FFF1 is the HUD rule, the immunity rim, the beam and nothing else. The app shown on the desk at 25.6 s is a recognisable likeness of the real product.

mandatory.customer_words: exact_text_strings — fifteen overlay strings, latin, may_reflow: false.
mandatory.realisation: All fifteen appear, verbatim, in the order supplied, every one composed by code in the text layer and none rendered by a generative model. No string is reflowed, retyped, abbreviated or translated. The two duplicate pairs are used as two distinct instances — the cheat code at 9.2 s and the closing ask at 28.6 s — which is what the duplication in the job record is for.

mandatory.customer_words: deliverable_request: aspect 9:16, count 1, kind multi_shot_story, modality video, motion from generated with audio true, seconds 30, operation generate, subject logo rentok_wordmark.
mandatory.realisation: One 9:16 film, 30 s, multi-shot, every drawn beat produced as a still then image-to-video and stitched by code; native audio on, with an original chiptune and in-world game sound and no voice-over. The subject of the deliverable is the wordmark, and the wordmark is what the last frame holds.

mandatory.customer_words: ambiguity_markers: kind_nearest_match: 30 s game-style advertising film, longer than the registered multi_shot_story band.
mandatory.realisation: Handled by structure rather than by more shots: nine beats, not a parade of scenes, with the single longest take in the film — 6.2 s — sitting in the middle where a 30 s cut usually fragments. The film therefore runs long against the registered band without changing its cutting rate.

brand_timeline.in_context: Before 9.2 s the brand is present only as its colour system — the cyan #03FFF1 HUD rule on the top edge of frame one and the coin and ground values — which is in-situ branding and not yet attributable, since the colour has not been tied to the product in a close shot. The mark itself arrives at 9.2 s composited onto the phone screen in the owner's hand, inside the ten-second window and carried by the product in use rather than by a card. It returns on the flag at the top of his own building at 22.9 s, as the live app on the real desk at 25.6 s, and as the supplied mark on the close card from 28.6 s to 30.0 s. Four appearances, four different asset types, none of them a repeat of another.
brand_timeline.spoken: none — the film carries no voice-over and no dialogue, so the brand name is never spoken. Declared as a deviation below; on Reels, Facebook and Shorts the on-screen channel carries the name and the ask alone.

last_frame: The code-composed close card, held still: flat #0038FF ground, the supplied rentok_wordmark unaltered in the upper-middle zone — Rent in white, Ok in cyan #03FFF1 — with INSTALL / RENTOK APP set beneath it in white at the card's largest size and RENTOK.COM smaller at the base of the type block, inside the bottom safe zone. Nothing moves; room tone runs under it and stops one frame before the end.

deviations.from: / default via ogx_0038: cartoons sell to children but are below average at changing brand preference with adults; the CHECK reads 'no cartoon for adults'.
deviations.brief_clause: "The video has a Mario game." plus "Game identity: An original Mario-inspired game" — the customer has specified the animated game form as the deliverable. Mitigated the way the source's own comparison suggests: the film ends by leaving the drawn world for a real desk and a real phone, so the last five seconds are live and the product is shown as itself.

deviations.from: default via ogx_0020: avoid analogies; readers do not complete the equation and the vehicle displaces the product.
deviations.brief_clause: "The obstacles in the game are basically the problems that owner faces — tenant verification, collecting rent..." — the brief is an analogy by construction. Mitigated per whip_0046 rather than hidden: the borrowed form is re-angled onto the product advantage instead of set beside the logo — the power-up is literally the app, the obstacles are literally the five named problems, and the vehicle is dismantled on screen at 25.6 s so the viewer is left holding the product, not the game.

deviations.from: / defaults via abcd_0021, abcd_0012 and ogx_0042: the on-screen CTA is voiced in the same words, the brand name is spoken as well as shown, and supers equal speech.
deviations.brief_clause: The job's standing constraint "no dialogue or voice-over", against delivery to "Instagram Reels / Facebook and YouTube Shorts". The source's own premise is that audio is heard, and it is stated for YouTube with sound on. Every pairing is therefore carried by the on-screen channel alone: the ask, the brand name and all five capability lines are composed text, and the film passes the muted test.

deviations.from: / default via abcd_0011: introduce the brand or product from the start and never let the presence lapse.
deviations.brief_clause: "The game also introduces a cheat code — install RentOK app. Once it is done, Mario gets a gun sort of power/immunity." — the brief's own structure withholds RentOK until the cheat code, and the film's deprivation act only works if the product is absent from it. The mark arrives at 9.2 s, inside ogx_0039's ten seconds, and the brand's colour system is on screen from frame one; from 9.2 s onward the presence never lapses again. abcd_0026's full-funnel row explicitly reorders what appears early and late, and it is the ordering used here.

deviations.from: / default via alb_0005: no running line in all-capitals, capitals being the hardest read.
deviations.brief_clause: exact_text_strings are supplied verbatim with "may_reflow": false — all fifteen are upper-case as given and may not be re-set. Mitigated within what is allowed: no chip exceeds three words, every chip is set in a wide-stroke face, and each is measured at 4.5:1 or better at both the darkest and the lightest point of its ground rather than taking any exemption.

deviations.from: / default via gote_0053: a shot that must be read holds its describe-aloud duration.
deviations.brief_clause: "Duration: 30 seconds" carrying fifteen mandated strings. Beat 6 is declared an action passage under gote_0052 and runs three tick chips at roughly 2.0 s each; the two chips in beat 2 run 0.9 s apart but are single hits on their own landings, not shots to be read. Every shot whose job is to be read — the lit phone at 9.2 s, the flag, the desk, the close card — holds 1.4 s or longer.

deviations.from: / : a cut that breaks established space names the higher criterion it keeps.
deviations.brief_clause: The cut at 25.6 s leaves the drawn world entirely for a live-action desk, which is a change of locale that gote_0037 would bound with a fade. It is taken as a straight match cut on the phone's screen position and size, with the sound changing one fraction ahead of the picture. The higher criteria kept are emotion and story: the recognition that the game was his own week only lands if the change is instant, and a fade at 25.6 s would cost two of the thirty seconds the brief fixes.

deviations.from: / default via ogx_0009: one specific figure — a percentage, a time, a sum — beats generalities.
deviations.brief_clause: The job record supplies no verified figure of any kind, and exact_text_strings are the only permitted claim words. No number is invented. The specificity is carried instead by the five named capabilities the customer supplied — DIGITAL KYC, AUTOPAY, DUES TRACKED LIVE, COMPLAINT TICKETS, ONE DASHBOARD — and by sensory detail in the picture. Flagged rather than faked.

deviations.from: via nnn_0012: ASCI Code compliance is outside Canon.
deviations.brief_clause: market IN. Every claim in the film is one of the customer's own supplied strings; none is comparative, superlative or quantified. ASCI Code check on all five capability strings is still required outside Canon before release, and is stated here rather than assumed.
